items.title: Hackers Hide Linux Backdoor in Control Web Panel Server to Execute Commands Without Logs
items.snippet: A backdoor has been found hiding in the web server that runs Control Web Panel (CWP), a free panel for managing Linux hosting servers, researchers at QiAnXin's XLab said this week. The backdoored web server executes commands that attackers send via web requests, and those requests never appear in its access logs. Installing it takes root access, so the attackers must already control the server.
items.summary: Attackers are hiding a Linux backdoor in Control Web Panel servers to execute unlogged remote commands. Control Web Panel administrators are affected. Inspect server access logs and monitor the panel for unauthorized modifications.

items.summary: Two vulnerabilities in Barracuda Email Security Gateway can be chained to achieve unauthenticated root access. Administrators of Barracuda appliances are affected. Apply the patches released on Monday.

items.summary: A remote code execution vulnerability in Windows Paint can be fixed via the Microsoft Store. Windows users are affected. Update Microsoft Paint to build 11.2609.401.0 or later via the Microsoft Store.

items.summary: Malicious browser extensions can abuse the Claude Dispatch feature to execute code on local machines. Developers using Claude Desktop and browser extensions are affected. Review and audit installed browser extensions that interact with AI web interfaces.

items.title: Installing the Fix for an Exploited WordPress Flaw Can Expose Some Sites One Last Time
items.snippet: Some WordPress sites can still be attacked while they install the fix for an actively exploited flaw, according to Umut Bayram, the Picus Security researcher who found it. The update that installs the fix still unpacks its files using the site's old, unpatched code, so an attacker who strikes at the right moment can run code on the server. The researcher advises blocking web access to the
items.summary: An actively exploited WordPress vulnerability can still leave some sites exposed during the installation of the fix itself. WordPress administrators should monitor site logs during updates. Upgrade WordPress to the latest patched version or follow vendor guidance.

items.title: Hackers Target OpenSSH SSHole Flaw Within Hours of Disclosure, Gain Root on Honeypot
items.snippet: Threat actors are attempting to exploit a recently disclosed security flaw impacting OpenSSH that can enable sign-ins to accounts that have no password set, according to Previdian. items.summary: Threat actors are actively targeting the SSHole flaw in OpenSSH which allows sign-ins to accounts without a password. Linux server administrators should review account configurations and ensure all accounts have passwords or keys. Upgrade OpenSSH to the latest version or apply patches.
items.bumpReason: Active exploitation in the wild warrants higher urgency.
